items.title: LibriSpeech-Real-QA: A Benchmark for Streaming Question Answering
items.summary_1line: Most speech large language models (SLMs) still process speech in an offline manner. They only start responding after they receive the complete speech segment. However, many real-world applications require streaming sp...
items.editor_note: Adds a benchmark for streaming speech QA, a new modality for the thread.

editorial.tldr: Late-October arXiv papers attacked question answering where plain LLM calls fall short: tables in document images and knowledge graphs without QA annotations. A multilingual multi-hop document QA paper then added agentic skills.
editorial.whats_new: LibriSpeech-Real-QA (Nov 4) is a benchmark for streaming question answering, where speech LLMs must respond before the full audio segment has arrived.
editorial.why_it_matters: These are research papers, not products, but they show QA moving toward iterative self-checking, agentic skills and streaming input, which change latency and eval design for pipelines.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat these as preprints: if you run document or speech QA, note the benchmarks they introduce and wait for independent reproductions before changing a pipeline.

beats.headline: Self-evaluation and self-evolution for table and knowledge-graph QA
DocSkill brings skill-integrated agents to multilingual multi-hop document QA

open_questions: Do any of these methods report results that hold up outside their own benchmarks?
Will speech LLMs show measurable accuracy loss when answering before the full audio arrives?
